name: Tableau
description: Tableau is a Salesforce-owned business intelligence and data visualization platform for connecting to data and building interactive dashboards, licensed by role (Viewer, Explorer, Creator) across Tableau Cloud, Server, or Desktop.
best_for: Analysts and BI teams that want deep, highly customizable visual analytics and are willing to license by role (Viewer/Explorer/Creator) rather than pay one flat per-user rate.
features: Drag-and-drop visual analytics for building interactive dashboards and worksheets
Tableau Desktop (Windows and Mac) for authoring, plus Tableau Cloud and Tableau Server for publishing and sharing
Role-based licensing — Viewer, Explorer, and Creator — matching cost to how much authoring power each person actually needs
Tableau Prep, included with a Creator license, for preparing and cleaning data before analysis
Tableau Agent, available to Creator and Explorer seats, for AI-assisted data preparation, calculation-building, and exploration
Tableau Mobile apps for iOS and Android, included with every license tier
Data-driven alerts and subscriptions so Viewers can be notified of changes without opening a workbook
pros: Role-based licensing (Viewer/Explorer/Creator) lets organizations pay less for people who only need to view or lightly edit dashboards
Tableau Agent brings AI-assisted data prep, calculation-building, and exploration into both Creator and Explorer seats
Tableau Desktop supports both Windows and Mac for authoring, unlike some competitors' Windows-only desktop tools
cons: Creator, the only role that includes full authoring plus Tableau Desktop and Prep, costs $75/user/month (Standard) or $115/user/month (Enterprise), several times the Viewer rate
Published per-user rates require annual billing

tiers.name: Viewer
tiers.notes: Standard edition, billed annually. Includes Tableau Mobile access, commenting, exporting, subscriptions, and data-driven alerts.

tiers.name: Explorer
tiers.notes: Standard edition, billed annually. Adds web-based workbook authoring/editing and Tableau Agent in web authoring.

tiers.name: Creator
tiers.notes: Standard edition, billed annually. Full authoring plus Tableau Desktop and Tableau Prep. Enterprise edition Creator is $115/user/month, billed annually.

alternatives.name: Microsoft Power BI
alternatives.description: Microsoft's BI platform, with simple per-user pricing and deep integration into Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Fabric.
alternatives.best_for: Teams already standardized on Microsoft 365 that want lower-cost per-user BI licensing rather than Tableau's role-based tiers.

faq.question: What's the difference between Tableau Viewer, Explorer, and Creator?
faq.answer: Viewer ($15/user/month) can view, comment on, and subscribe to dashboards via web or Tableau Mobile. Explorer ($42/user/month) adds web-based authoring and editing. Creator ($75/user/month, Standard edition) adds full authoring plus Tableau Desktop and Tableau Prep. All prices are billed annually.

faq.question: Does Tableau have a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes, Tableau offers a 14-day free trial that can be used without restrictions before a product key or Tableau Cloud sign-in is required.

faq.question: Is there a genuinely free Tableau plan?
faq.answer: No. Tableau does not offer a perpetual free tier for its core product; every license (Viewer, Explorer, Creator) is paid, with only a 14-day trial available at no cost.
